definitions.gloss: to take up a position; to station oneself; to claim a spot
definitions.explanation: To settle into a particular location and occupy it, often implying staying there for some time. Originally a military term meaning to set up camp, now commonly used for everyday situations like claiming a seat or spot.

examples.japanese: ⟦{窓際|まどぎわ}→窓際：08400_madogiwa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{陣取|じんど}った。
examples.english: I claimed a spot by the window.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦テレビ→テレビ：01536_terebi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{陣取|じんど}って⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: The children have planted themselves in front of the TV.

examples.japanese: ⟦{花見|はなみ}→花見：01700_hanami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{場所|ばしょ}→場所：00829_basho⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{確保|かくほ}→確保：13681_kakuho⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{陣取|じんど}って⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧がいた。
examples.english: There were people who had been camped out in the park since morning to secure a spot for cherry blossom viewing.

notes:
A godan verb ({五段動詞|ごだんどうし}) conjugating with the る row. Originally a military term from ⟦{陣|じん}→陣：30535_jin⟧ (battle formation/camp) + ⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ (to take), it has shifted to everyday use describing someone settling firmly into a spot.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{窓際|まどぎわ}→窓際：08400_madogiwa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{陣取|じんど}る (claim a window seat)
- ⟦テレビ→テレビ：01536_terebi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{陣取|じんど}る (plant oneself in front of the TV)
- ⟦{最前列|さいぜんれつ}→最前列：17707_saizenretsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{陣取|じんど}る (take up a front-row position)

USAGE:
Implies staying put for a while, not just briefly sitting. Often carries a humorous or slightly exaggerated tone in everyday speech, as if the person is "occupying" a position like a soldier. The て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ form is especially common, emphasizing the ongoing occupation of the spot.
